issues.issue: Were the appellants given enough advance notice that IFA was in issue and of Benin City and Port Harcourt?
issues.applicant_position: No advance notice of IFA or of the proposed cities, so they could not bring evidence on those cities.
issues.result_quote: I found no breaches of procedural fairness in this matter.

issues.issue: Did the RPD err by applying the Jurisprudential Guide on IFA and by not considering indigeneship?
issues.applicant_position: JG IFA does not fit their facts and does not consider indigeneship, which they say is central in Nigeria.
issues.result_quote: For these reasons, I find that the RPD did not err by considering the JG IFA.

issues.issue: Do the appellants have a safe internal flight alternative (first prong of the IFA test)?
issues.applicant_position: Agents can find them through social media; family is motivated to find them and the Principal Appellant has an elevated profile.
issues.result_quote: I find that the Appellants have established, on a balance of probabilities, that they do not have a safe IFA.

issues.issue: Is relocation to the IFA unreasonable or unduly harsh (second prong of the IFA test)?
issues.result_quote: As the first prong of the IFA test has failed, I will not proceed to the second prong of the test.

issues.issue: Have the appellants established a risk of FGM and facial scarring in Nigeria, so as to be Convention refugees?
issues.applicant_position: Family wants FGM for the daughters and facial scarring; refusal brings ostracism, blackmail and abuse.
issues.result_quote: I find that the Appellants have established their claims that they are at risk in Nigeria.
